gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in a peer-reviewed field trial (Gaskamp et al., Animals, 2021), traps watched by a cellular camera and closed remotely by the trapper (suspended traps) removed 88.1% of the estimated wild-pig population at 0.64 person-hours per pig, while trip-wire corral traps removed 48.5% at 2.3 person-hours per pig.
standout_why: I compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited: jagerpro.com/product/m-i-n-e-live-stream-camera-system, hogeyecameras.com and hogtraptrigger.com. I also read HogEye's own blog post on capture rates. None has a measurement by a named third party. JAGER PRO lists only its own specs: a 1.2 s trigger time and power-use figures. HogEye gives unattributed claims: '50 notifications dropped to 3' and, from an unnamed land manager, 'capture rates increased by 40%+'. Hog Trap Trigger has no figures; it only says you can tell 'within a minute or so' whether hogs are in the trap. Peer-reviewed numbers comparing a remotely triggered trap with a trip-wire trap appear on none of them.
decides: The studies back ChatGPT's main advice with named numbers: a trap that lets you watch on camera and close the gate when the whole group is inside catches more pigs, with fewer hours, than a trip wire. They do not rank the brands. No named lab or reviewer has measured the JAGER PRO, HogEye, Hog Trap Trigger or AnywhereCam systems. So the choice between them has to rest on price, plan cost, gate compatibility and cell coverage. The data also suggest that seeing the whole group live before you close the gate matters more than trigger speed.
candidates: JAGER PRO M.I.N.E. Live Stream Camera

findings.label: Share of the estimated wild-pig population removed, by trap type
findings.value: Suspended trap, cellular camera, closed remotely by the trapper: 88.1%; drop net, line-of-sight remote: 85.7%; corral trap, trip wire: 48.5%
findings.source_title: Gaskamp, Gee, Campbell, Silvy & Webb, 'Effectiveness and Efficiency of Corral Traps, Drop Nets and Suspended Traps for Capturing Wild Pigs (Sus scrofa)', Animals 11(6):1565, published 2021-05-27
findings.note: Texas ranch field trials, 601 pigs removed in total. The suspended traps used a 3G cellular webcam that texted images; the trapper looked and then dropped the trap remotely. The paper names no commercial trap brand. Corral traps per year: 60.6% (2010) and 36.4% (2011).

findings.label: Labor per pig caught (person-hours per pig)
findings.value: Suspended trap with cellular remote: 0.64 h; drop net: 1.9 h; trip-wire corral: 2.3 h
findings.note: Same study. Total hours were 2.92 for the suspended traps, 9.79 for drop nets and 7.2 for corral traps. Setup took 0.76 person-hours for a suspended trap and 2.6 for a corral trap.

findings.label: Pigs caught per capture event
findings.value: Suspended trap with cellular remote: mean 8.2 (SD 7.9), largest catch 30; trip-wire corral: mean 3.9 (SD 3.7), largest 14; drop net: mean 9.6 (SD 9.0), largest 27
findings.note: The authors report the average group caught was 2.1 times larger with suspended traps than with corral traps. Escapes: 8 from suspended traps, 11 from corral traps, 29 from drop nets.

findings.label: Equipment and data cost in that trial
findings.value: Suspended trap about $1,500 including the cellular kit, plus $50/month for cellular data; corral trap about $500; drop net about $3,500
findings.note: Costs are from around 2011 and were not adjusted for inflation. They are context only, not today's prices.

findings.label: Change in pig density: whole-group ('smart' trap) removal vs traditional control
findings.value: Whole-group removal: density fell 53% after year 1 and held in year 2. Traditional control: no significant change after trapping. Median removal rate 42.5% vs 0.0% in 2018 and 29.6% vs 5.3% in 2019
findings.source_title: Europe PMC record: Kilgo, Vukovich, Cox, Larsen, Mims & Garabedian, 'Assessing whole-sounder removal versus traditional control for reducing invasive wild pig (Sus scrofa) populations', Pest Management Science 79(9):3033-3042, online 2023-04-08
findings.note: USDA Forest Service study at a Department of Energy site in South Carolina, run over two years. The abstract names no brand and says whole-group removal takes more time and money.

findings.label: Whole-group catch rate across 867 professional capture events
findings.value: Every trap type (corral, drop, passive net) removed all targeted pigs in at least 88% of capture events
findings.source_title: UGA Savannah River Ecology Lab, 'Wild Pig Management and the Science Behind Trapping' by Tyjaha Steele, 2025-03-10, on Taylor, Buxton & Beasley, Wildlife Society Bulletin 49(1), 2025-01-19
findings.note: 31 professional trappers in four southeastern US states. With professional operators, the gap between trap types was small. No brands are named.

findings.product: JAGER PRO M.I.N.E. Live Stream Camera
findings.label: Trigger time and power use (stated by the maker, not independently measured)
findings.value: Trigger time 1.2 s; resting power 0.84 mW; daytime use 45.36 Ws; nighttime use 49.35 Ws; IR flash range 60 ft
findings.source_title: Hog Trap Camera with Remote Trigger | M.I.N.E.® Live Stream - JAGER PRO
